memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "When a calf, a lamb or a goat is born, it is
to remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it
will be acceptable as a food offering presented to the LORD"
- Lev 22:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A newborn animal was to stay with its mother for a full week before it
could be offered. There was no ritual necessity for this. It simply
reflects something about the God who gave the command.

He notices the bond between a mother and her young. He builds a small
kindness into the middle of a sacrificial system. Even here, in the
regulations about slaughter, there is restraint and gentleness.

Scripture says the righteous care for the needs of their animals (Prov
12:10). Jesus said not one sparrow falls to the ground outside the
Father's care (Matt 10:29). The God of the Bible is not indifferent to
His creation.

Dear reader, if God attends to a newborn lamb and its mother, how much
more does He attend to you? Jesus made that exact argument. If God
feeds the birds and clothes the wild flowers, are you not much more
valuable than they (Matt 6:26-30)?

Sometimes we carry the quiet fear that our concerns are too small to
bother God with. Leviticus 22 gently disagrees. The God who legislated
a week of mother's milk for a calf is not too busy for what is
troubling you today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "small" concern have I been hesitant to bring to God?
2. How does God's care for creation reassure me about His care for me?
3. Am I gentle with the creatures and people in my care?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that no detail is beneath Your notice. I bring You
the small worries I have been carrying alone, trusting Your kindness.
Amen.
